correctness.rationale: For n>=4 all quantifiers, closed-neighbourhood conventions, and boundary part sizes are explicit. Any dominating set projects to a pair family hitting every 3-subset of B; one added pair per selected layer-zero triple costs no more than the selected vertex count. The complementary pair graph is triangle-free and an elementary Mantel proof gives t_n. The explicitly defined disjoint three-layer witness has t_n+n-2 vertices and covers each of the three classes by direct adjacency. Independent stdlib script verify.py checked every vertex for n=4,...,18 and exhaustive Mantel small n=2,...,6; checked check_output.json matches its replay. Squeezing gives 1/4 and no exact gamma(n) claim is made.

value.rationale: The targeted high-token bipartite domination question has much looser literature bounds; here a simple graph-layer projection proves an unavoidable quadratic lower bound and a three-layer witness gives a quadratic upper with identical sharp coefficient 1/4. Relative to the current general bipartite k>=3 result, the upper order drops from cubic to quadratic and the quadratic lower coefficient triples. This is a motivated, infinite, asymptotically exact determination of a natural invariant, not a random finite slice or renaming.
